approach: Add crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs. It lists the programs a capability's checks run, looks each bare name up on PATH through an injectable `ToolProbe` (the system probe scans PATH and runs nothing), and returns every program considered plus blockers, each with a non-empty workaround. Path-named programs are listed as "not probed (path)", never silently dropped. `Athena::dispatch` (run/mod.rs) calls it right after `capability.checks(&jc)`, writes one line per program into the existing `Job.note` (committed in the prediction commit before any agent runs), and on a blocker closes the job `failed` with an `environment: preflight blocked: ...` reason before the resume, planning and producer branches, leaving an earlier job's kept work alone. A small pure function follows a 'try again on' link through a preflight stop so a drain retry still reaches the earlier job's kept work. The spec entry and one CHANGELOG line follow. This revision corrects the premise: today a job whose check program cannot start LANDS, with the baseline failure recorded as pre-existing (checks.rs:541-562; lifecycle.rs:150-152). The preflight deliberately turns that into an environment stop for bare-name programs; the plan says so everywhere, limits the 0% estimate to this repository's checks, and applies one rule to path programs (not probed, listed as such). New tests are all named `capability_preflight_*` so the filter selects only them.

decisions.choice: Needed programs are the first element of each check's `run`, each listed once with the names of the checks that need it. A bare name (non-empty, no `/`) is probed. A path-named program (contains `/`) is NOT probed and is recorded in the note as `<path>: not probed (path)`. Git, gh and the agent binary are not added as needs of their own.
decisions.reason: Finding 2 (premise corrected). Today a check program that cannot start is not a failure of the job: checks.rs:541-562 turns the spawn error into a failed CheckRun with the note 'could not start', and lifecycle.rs:128-152 asserts the job still lands because the same failure is pre-existing on the base. So the preflight is a deliberate behavior change for bare-name programs: such a job now stops with an environment reason instead of landing. One rule for paths: a path program resolves against the check's working directory (a relative path may name a file the producer creates) or an absolute location Athena does not control, so Athena cannot decide in advance that it is a missing capability; it is recorded as not probed, with the reason, rather than dropped. The lifecycle test is therefore NOT evidence that only missing tools refuse; it only pins that path programs are outside the preflight. Git: Athena runs git before the hook (`JobConfig::at(&self.git, head)` run/mod.rs:1029, `pin_repo` 1100, the prediction commit 1261), so a git blocker could not be recorded; a check that runs `git` is still probed as a check program. gh never changes a job's outcome (gh/early.rs:425-437 only warns) and `athena land` is a later command. The agent binary belongs to the driver trait object that tests replace.

rejected.option: Probe path programs too (a file exists with an execute bit) and rewrite `baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job` to use a program that exists but fails
rejected.why: A relative path may name a file the producer creates, so it cannot be judged before the producer runs; the rewrite would also stop testing the 'could not start' baseline path (lifecycle.rs:148-149) and add a file outside the deliverables for no extra evidence about tools on PATH.
Left a missing program unrecorded, against 'checks and records each needed capability', and justified itself with a wrong premise about the lifecycle test.
Unreachable: a missing git fails earlier with no record.

decisions.choice: `SystemProbe { path: Option<OsString> }` answers 'is the bare name an executable file in a PATH entry' by scanning `std::env::split_paths`, skipping empty entries; a candidate counts when `std::fs::metadata` says file with any execute bit (unix). It runs nothing. Trait `ToolProbe` has one method `present(&self, tool: &str) -> bool`; `from_env()` and `with_path(..)` for tests. Two stated limits in the doc comment and in the spec mechanism: (1) it reads Athena's own PATH, while checks run with `env_clear().envs(ctx.env)` (checks.rs:534-535), an environment built from `env_pass` plus the capability's `env` templates (athena-agent/src/env.rs:70-74, 101-109), which could set PATH; (2) 'any execute bit' is looser than the kernel's check for the current user.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: this repository passes PATH (athena.toml:52 `env_pass = ["HOME", "PATH"]`) and sets no PATH template, so the probe and the check agree here; a repository whose capability `env` sets PATH can disagree, and the plan states that limit instead of re-implementing the env build inside athena-core (the capability env is not available at the hook). A PATH scan is what `Command::new` does and has no side effects; running `<tool> --version` would run whatever script athena.toml names, can hang, and a kill leaves grandchildren. This replaces the `--version` run in the accepted reading and keeps its aim, a probe a test can inject. athena-core has no libc/rustix dependency for `access(X_OK)`.

rejected.option: Build the probe's PATH from the capability env templates at the hook
rejected.why: The env is built per side and job directory inside athena-agent; reaching it from the hook widens the change beyond the deliverables.
Side effects, up to 5 s per tool, grandchildren stay running.
New dependency for a rare mismatch.

decisions.choice: No new field on Athena and no test seam: pure `preflight(&[Need], &dyn ToolProbe)` takes the probe as an argument (unit tests pass `FakeProbe`); `check_tools(&[CheckSpec])` is the production entry and builds `SystemProbe::from_env()`. Dispatch tests use the real probe: bare-name program `athena-preflight-absent-tool` (on no PATH) for missing, `true` for present.
decisions.reason: `Athena` is built by struct literal in about 67 places across 41 files; a new field would touch files far outside the deliverables.

decisions.choice: Record the preflight in the existing `Job.note` (Option<String>, athena-data/src/records.rs:625), set at the Job literal (run/mod.rs:1250, now `None`), committed in the prediction commit (1261) before any agent runs. One line per program: `<tool>: present`, `<tool>: missing` or `<path>: not probed (path)`, each followed by `needed by <checks>`; with no check programs the note is `no check programs to probe`. The blocker and workaround are also in the closing outcome reason. Finding 5 stated plainly: nothing reads or prints `Job.note` (status.rs and display.rs do not), so the full per-tool record is visible only in the job's job.json; the stop reason is the only part a command shows, and only for a blocked job. The spec mechanism says this, so the verifier knows where 'records each needed capability' is shown (job.json `note`, asserted by tests at `finished.prediction_commit`).

The deliverable list names pin.rs; the producer reports it as an unchanged planned file with this reason.

decisions.choice: A blocked job keeps an earlier job's work: `dispatch` computes `earlier` (job of `retry_seed`, `resume`, `resume_from` or `stale_conflict`) before the context is built; on a blocker the context is built with `resume: None`, so `close_dispatched` does not call `remove_kept_work` (run/close.rs:152-154) and `settle_resume_marks` (run/mod.rs:860-874) leaves the mark alone.
decisions.reason: A stop that did none of the work must not destroy the earlier job's kept work.

decisions.choice: New free function `through_preflight_stops(records, request) -> String` in run/mod.rs: while the job named by `retried_job(records, request)` closed with a preflight reason (`preflight::is_preflight_reason`) and its own request is a 'try again on' request, return that job's request instead (at most 16 hops). `dispatch` passes the result to `tree_seed`, `timeout_seed`, `resume_seed`, `stale_seed`, `retry_findings` and `planning_resume_seed`; `pin_repo` and the stored request keep the original text. Finding 4, limit stated: only `dispatch` follows the link. `Athena::retry` and `ask` (reading.rs:1220-1232) still read the raw 'try again on J2' text, so the reader of J3 sees J2's preflight stop and not J1's context; and `retries_by_job` (reading/retry.rs:246-268) leaves out only Dropped, Declined, Abandoned, Stale and Closed, so the Failed preflight stop J2 stands as J1's retry in `retry_follow_up` (retry.rs:272) status follow-ups. Both are unchanged and accepted: they are display and reader context, not work lost; the work (kept directory, mark, candidate) is reached through the dispatch follow.
decisions.reason: The drain's second attempt is `athena retry <last job>` (drain.rs:222-227); `timeout_seed` and `resume_seed` read only the directly retried job (run/mod.rs:888-896, 542). Without the follow, a retry of a preflight-stopped job would plan and produce from scratch and lose J1's kept work. For any non-preflight chain the text is unchanged.

risks.risk: Behavior change (finding 2): a job whose bare-name check program is absent landed before, with a recorded pre-existing failure (checks.rs:541-562; lifecycle.rs:150-152); now it stops `failed` (environment). In a repository with an uninstalled check tool, drains replace landings with stops, and the drain keeps reading and retrying such items because a preflight stop is OtherEnvironment and drain.rs:2706-2711 ends the run only for ProducerAuth and LowDisk (UsageLimit earlier).
risks.mitigation: This is the intended stricter behavior (criterion 5), stated in the spec mechanism and the CHANGELOG line. The reason names the tool and a workaround. The 0% newly-refused estimate holds only for this repository (all six configured checks run `cargo`, athena.toml:85-125; an estimate by reading). A follow-up outside these deliverables is to make a preflight stop end the drain like LowDisk.

risks.risk: The accepted reading assumed the probe runs `<tool> --version`; the plan looks the name up on PATH.
risks.mitigation: The injectable probe trait the reading asked for is kept; a PATH scan is what `Command::new` does and runs nothing. Stated in decision 2, the steps and the spec mechanism.

risks.risk: The reading named git as a probed tool; the plan does not probe it on its own.
risks.mitigation: Athena runs git at run/mod.rs:1029, 1100 and 1261, before the hook and with no record, so a git blocker could never be recorded. The spec mechanism and a code comment say so; a check that runs `git` is probed as a check program.

risks.risk: Probe PATH can disagree with the PATH the checks run with (finding 3): checks run with a cleared environment rebuilt from `env_pass` and capability `env` templates (checks.rs:534-535; env.rs:70-74, 101-109).
risks.mitigation: Equal in this repository (PATH passed, no PATH template). The limit is stated in the SystemProbe doc comment and the spec mechanism; the worst effect is a wrong block or the same late failure as today.

risks.risk: 'Any execute bit' is looser than the kernel's check for the current user; a 0700 file owned by another user passes the probe but cannot run.
risks.mitigation: Rare; the tool then fails at its check as today. athena-core has no libc/rustix dependency for `access(X_OK)`. Stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The per-tool record is only in job.json `note`; no command prints it (finding 5).
risks.mitigation: Stated in the spec mechanism; tests read it at `finished.prediction_commit`. Only the stop reason is shown to a user, and only for a blocked job. A status line is out of scope.

risks.risk: The reader of a follow-up retry and `retries_by_job`/`retry_follow_up` see the preflight-stopped job, not the job it retried (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: Only `dispatch` follows the link (decision 7); the work itself is reached through that follow and covered by test D. The limit is listed in dependents.

risks.risk: The filter `preflight` also matches existing budget-preflight tests (finding 6).
risks.mitigation: Every new test is named `capability_preflight_*`; the measure and all demonstration commands use that prefix or the full test name.

risks.risk: run/pin.rs is listed in the brief's deliverables but left unchanged, and the unchanged-planned-files check may send the job back.
risks.mitigation: The stop needs the private `Closing` and `RunContext`; if the check fires, the report lists pin.rs under `unchanged_planned_files` with that reason.

risks.risk: The new `Job.note` makes job.json differ from fixtures of tests that compare whole records.
risks.mitigation: Searched the crates for whole-record comparisons of `note: None` on Job and found none; `cargo test --locked` (athena-cli suites included) would show any.

risks.risk: Some existing test elsewhere configures a bare-name check program that is not on PATH and expects the job to proceed.
risks.mitigation: Step 9 runs the whole `cargo test --locked`; known programs in lifecycle, run tests and pin tests are `sh`, `true`, `cargo`, `git`, `grep`. Any failure is fixed by using a present program in that test, not by weakening the preflight.

risks.risk: Tests C and D build several Athena values over one repo and state directory.
risks.mitigation: `athena_with` derives the state path from the tempdir (tests.rs:198) and existing tests already retry through `athena.retry` then `go` (tests.rs:3707, 3770). If a second instance does not see the first's records, use one Athena whose check list changes through a shared cell.

risks.risk: `through_preflight_stops` changes which job a retry of a preflight-stopped job seeds from; a person might not expect J1.
risks.mitigation: Applies only when J2 closed with the `environment: preflight blocked:` reason (J2 did no work). One shared constant, cap of 16 hops, and test D asserts the brief names the job retried.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `capability_preflight_spec_entry_names_this_file_owner_and_test` in preflight.rs, shaped like `iris_spec_entry_names_files_that_exist` (iris.rs:227-243). It parses the real spec with `crate::hestia::parse_spec(include_str!("../../../docs/spec.toml"))`, finds OLY-B-RUN-01, and asserts: active, owner `Athena`, mechanism contains `crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs`, measure contains `capability_preflight_missing_tool_becomes_a_blocker_with_a_workaround_plan` and ends with `status: not shown`, `hestia::measure_problem(&measure)` is None, `hestia::spec_gaps(..)` has no gap for OLY-B-RUN-01, and that the preflight.rs file exists under `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../..`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_spec_entry && cargo test -p athena-core the_real_spec_records_every_field && git diff -- docs/spec.toml
demonstrations.observes: Both tests pass. The diff changes only OLY-B-RUN-01 (docs/spec.toml:2292-2296): mechanism from `none` to text naming preflight.rs and the run/mod.rs hook, saying bare-name check programs are probed on Athena's own PATH, path-named programs are recorded as not probed, git is checked earlier by Athena's own use, gh and the agent binary are not probed, and the per-tool record is only in job.json `note`; `owner = "Athena"`; a measure naming the specific test and ending `status: not shown`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the spec entry unchanged the mechanism is `none` and the measure ends `status: requirement`. The existing hestia test accepts that (hestia.rs:4293), but the new test fails on its own assertions: no preflight.rs in the mechanism, no test name in the measure, no `status: not shown` ending, and `spec_gaps` still lists OLY-B-RUN-01.
demonstrations.seam: No double. Production `hestia::parse_spec` (hestia.rs:1172), `measure_problem` (1219) and `spec_gaps` (1291) read the real docs/spec.toml through include_str!. They exist today; the test is added by plan step 6.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in preflight.rs call production `preflight::preflight(&needs, &probe)` and `needed_tools(&checks)`. The fake `FakeProbe { missing: Vec<&str> }` only answers present/missing per name and is passed as an argument. `capability_preflight_missing_tool_becomes_a_blocker_with_a_workaround_plan`: checks `["cargo","fmt"]` and `["cargo","test"]`, FakeProbe missing `cargo`; asserts exactly one blocker with tool `cargo`, `needed_by` listing both check names, a non-empty workaround, a note containing `cargo: missing`, and `stop_reason(None)` starting `environment: preflight blocked:` and naming `cargo` and `workaround`. `capability_preflight_all_tools_present_gives_no_blocker`: same needs, nothing missing; no blockers, `stop_reason(None) == None`, every tool in `checked` and in the note as `present`. Also: `capability_preflight_lists_path_programs_as_not_probed` (a path program is in `checked` as not probed, in the note as `not probed (path)`, never a blocker even with a probe that reports everything missing; an empty `run` is no need), `capability_preflight_shared_tool_listed_once`, `capability_preflight_needs_come_from_the_capability_checks` (specs shaped like athena.toml's cargo fmt/clippy/test give exactly `cargo`; a check running `git` gives `git`), `capability_preflight_git_alone_and_gh_are_not_needs`, `capability_preflight_stop_reason_names_the_earlier_job`, `capability_preflight_system_probe_finds_only_executable_files_on_path` (temp dir with an executable and a non-executable file via `SystemProbe::with_path`; empty PATH entry skipped).
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_missing_tool && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_all_tools_present && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight
demonstrations.observes: All pass. The missing-tool test shows one blocker naming `cargo` with a non-empty workaround; the all-present test shows none. The broad filter `capability_preflight` selects only the new tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the body of `preflight()` is stubbed to return an empty `Preflight`, the missing-tool test fails (0 blockers not 1, no `cargo: missing` line, `stop_reason` None) and the all-present assertions on `checked` fail. Reviewed in the diff.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `preflight::preflight(&[Need], &dyn ToolProbe)` and `needed_tools`, added by plan step 1. `FakeProbe` is injected as a function argument and answers only present/missing; blocker, workaround and note logic stay in production code. The real `SystemProbe` is exercised in one test through `with_path`.

demonstrations.method: Dispatch tests in run/tests.rs go through `Athena::go` into `dispatch` (run/mod.rs:402, 1015) with the existing harness (`repo()`, `athena_with(&repo,&state,check,plenty_of_space,script)`, `finished_job`, `counting`, `producer_ending`, Docs capability, tests.rs:90-215). Guards before the hook: paused-line check (mod.rs:1026), configuration-hash match (1030), `disk_gate`/`start_hold` (tests use `plenty_of_space`), budget reserve (1095), `pin_repo` (Docs does not pin). TEST A `capability_preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool_before_the_producer_and_records_it`: check `&["athena-preflight-absent-tool"]`, script `counting(counts, None)`; asserts Failed, a reason starting `environment: preflight blocked:` naming the tool and `workaround`, `is_environment_reason`, `StopCause::of == OtherEnvironment`, zero producer and verifier calls, and, loading `Records` at `finished.prediction_commit`, a Job `note` containing `athena-preflight-absent-tool: missing`, no candidate yet. TEST B `capability_preflight_records_every_probed_tool_when_all_are_present`: check `PASSES` (`true`); asserts the producer ran once, the reason does not start with `environment:`, and the Job record at `finished.prediction_commit` (before any candidate, showing the order) has a note containing `true: present`; a variant with a second check named by path also shows its `not probed (path)` line in the note. TEST C `capability_preflight_stop_on_a_resumed_retry_keeps_the_earlier_work`: a first Athena with `producer_ending(Error, &expired_login(), true, ..)` closes failed with a login-expiry stop and keeps a candidate commit but no kept directory (tests.rs:5368-5369), so after `finished_job` the test creates `athena.state.kept_work_dir(&first)` by hand with `create_dir_all` (as tests.rs:5249-5250). A second Athena over the same repo and state tempdirs (`athena_with`) has check `athena-preflight-absent-tool`; `retry(first)` then `go`. Asserts: Failed with the preflight reason naming `first`; `kept_work_dir(&first)` still exists; the first job's candidate commit is still in the repository; `timeout_seed(&records,"try again on <first>",&head)` still returns Some. TEST D `capability_preflight_retry_of_a_stopped_job_resumes_the_job_it_retried`: a third Athena with check `PASSES` runs `retry(stopped)` then `go`; asserts the job finishes, the producer ran once, the dispatch commit's producer brief names `first` as the job retried and carries the first job's progress note, and `kept_work_dir(&first)` is gone. Unit test `capability_preflight_follows_the_retry_link_through_a_stop` on `through_preflight_stops`: a request retrying a preflight-stopped job returns that job's own request; a chain of two collapses to the first; a request retrying a job closed any other way, or a stopped job whose own request is not a retry, is returned unchanged.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_records_every_probed_tool && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_stop_on_a_resumed_retry && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_retry_of_a_stopped_job && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_follows_the_retry_link && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: A: Failed with the environment reason, no producer call, blocker in the note and the outcome. B: the producer ran and the note lists each probed program, recorded in the prediction commit. C: the stop names the earlier job; its kept directory and candidate survive. D: a retry of the stopped job resumes the first job's work and consumes its kept directory. The last command runs the whole crate.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hook is removed or runs after the producer, A fails (the producer runs, reason not environment). If `Job.note` is not set, A and B fail on the note assertions. If the context keeps `resume` on a blocked job, C fails because close.rs:152-154 removes `kept/<first>`. If `through_preflight_stops` is not applied in dispatch, D fails: the third job plans from scratch, its brief does not name `first`, and the kept directory stays.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs:402) into `dispatch` (1015) plus the new free function `through_preflight_stops`. Fixtures: `FakeAgentDriver` with a script, the Docs capability and a temp repo, all existing in run/tests.rs. The preflight uses the real `SystemProbe` on the process PATH: `true` exists there, `athena-preflight-absent-tool` does not; no injection needed. C and D build further `Athena` values over the same tempdirs through `athena_with`, which derives the state path from the tempdir (tests.rs:198). Tests are added by plan step 7.

demonstrations.method: Show the stricter behavior is intended and bounded. (1) Test A: a job whose bare-name check program is absent is refused (this is the newly refused case; today it lands with a pre-existing failure, checks.rs:541-562). (2) Test B: with the program present the job proceeds and records it. (3) `capability_preflight_lists_path_programs_as_not_probed` and `capability_preflight_git_alone_and_gh_are_not_needs` show the need list holds only check programs, with paths listed as not probed. (4) The unchanged lifecycle test `baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job` (lifecycle.rs:129-152) still lands a job whose check is a missing path; it pins that path programs are outside the preflight, not that only missing tools refuse. The 0% newly-refused figure is an estimate by reading, limited to this repository's checks: all six in athena.toml (lines 85, 91, 99, 116, 120, 125) run `cargo`. For a repository with an uninstalled bare-name check tool the share is not zero and is intended.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_records_every_probed_tool && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_lists_path_programs && cargo test -p athena-core capability_preflight_git_alone_and_gh_are_not_needs
